# Enchantment Extraction

## Overview
Extraction safety and quality improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have learned the dangerous art of dismantling magical enchantments to uncover the secrets hidden within them.

By flooding an enchanted item with mana and carefully destabilising its enchantment matrix, you may extract fragments of magical knowledge before the enchantment collapses. The process is destructive, unpredictable, and often dangerous.

Whether successful or not, the enchanted item is permanently destroyed.

Only enchantments associated with magical elements known to the Artificer can be studied in this manner.

---

### Effects

- Spend **50 MP** to attempt an **Enchantment Extraction**.
- The enchanted item is **destroyed regardless of success or failure**.
- You may only attempt to extract enchantments associated with magical elements you know.
- Artificers normally know a maximum of **3 magical elements**.
- Make an **Enchantment Extraction Roll**.
- Gain **+2** to all Enchantment Extraction Rolls.
- On success:
  - Gain **1 Knowledge Fragment** for the extracted enchantment.
- On Critical Success:
  - Gain **2 Knowledge Fragments** for the extracted enchantment.
- Once the required number of Knowledge Fragments has been collected, the enchantment is permanently learned.
- Learned enchantments may later be used through the Enchanting Profession system.

### Extraction Difficulty

| Enchantment Rank | DC |
|---|---:|
| Weak | 10 |
| Minor | 13 |
| Greater | 16 |
| Strengthened | 19 |
| Enhanced | 24 |
| Superior | 28 |
| Grand | 33 |
| World | 40 |

### Knowledge Fragments Required

| Enchantment Rank | Fragments Required |
|---|---:|
| Weak | 1 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Greater | 3 |
| Strengthened | 5 |
| Enhanced | 10 |
| Superior | 20 |
| Grand | 50 |
| World | 100* |

\*World Enchantments may require additional research, quests, discoveries, or GM approval before they can be fully learned.

### Enchantment Backlash

If the extraction fails, the enchantment matrix collapses violently.

| Greater | 3D6 | -2 | 8 Hours |
| Strengthened | 4D6 | -2 | 12 Hours |
| Enhanced | 5D6 | -3 | 24 Hours |
| Superior | 6D6 | -3 | 1 Day |
| Grand | 8D6 | -4 | 2 Days |
| World | 10D6 | -5 | 2 Days |

---

Most Enchanters learn through study.

Artificers often learn through experimentation.

Enchantment Extraction was originally developed by Artificers frustrated by the slow pace of traditional magical education. By sacrificing enchanted items, they discovered they could study enchantment patterns directly from the source.

The process remains controversial among magical scholars, who view the destruction of enchanted items as reckless and wasteful.

Artificers simply call it efficient.

---

> *"A broken enchantment still has something to teach. The question is whether you're willing to pay the price."*  
>  **Rune-Savant Elric Voss**

Some lessons are earned through success.

Others are learned through pain.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have learned how to dismantle crafted objects and alchemical creations in order to understand how they were made.

By carefully deconstructing an item while flooding its internal structure with mana, you can uncover fragments of knowledge hidden within its design. Through repeated study and experimentation, these fragments can eventually be assembled into a complete schematic or formula.

The process is destructive.

Whether successful or not, the item is permanently destroyed.

To most craftsmen this would be considered wasteful.

To an Artificer, it is education.

---

- Gain **+10** to all Reverse Engineering Rolls.
- On Success:
  - Gain **1 Knowledge Fragment**.
- On Critical Success:
  - Gain **4 Knowledge Fragments**.
- Once the required number of Knowledge Fragments has been collected, the schematic or formula is permanently learned.
- Learned schematics may be crafted through their respective crafting professions.
- Learned potion formulas may be brewed through the Alchemy profession.

### Eligible Targets

- Crafted Equipment
- Weapons
- Armour
- Tools
- Gadgets
- Constructs
- Potions
- Crafting Schematics
- Formula-Based Items

---

### Schematic Difficulty

| Schematic Tier | DC | Fragments Required |
|---|---:|---:|
| Simple | 10 | 1 |
| Advanced | 13 | 2 |
| Innovated | 16 | 3 |
| Ingenious | 19 | 5 |
| Cutting Edge | 24 | 8 |
| Revolutionary | 28 | 12 |
| Masterwork | 33 | 16 |
| Savant | 40 | 20* |

---

### Potion Formula Difficulty

| Potion Level | DC | Fragments Required |
|---|---:|---:|
| Basic | 10 | 1 |
| Brew | 13 | 2 |
| Tincture | 16 | 3 |
| Suspension | 19 | 5 |
| Concoction | 24 | 8 |
| Solution | 28 | 12 |
| Infused | 33 | 16 |
| Elixir | 40 | 20* |

\*Savant Schematics and Elixir Formulas may require additional research, experimentation, rare materials, field testing, quests, discoveries, or GM approval before they can be fully learned.

---

### Reverse Engineering Backlash

If the attempt fails, the item collapses into unstable fragments, releasing harmful feedback.

| Tier | Damage | Intelligence Check Penalty | Duration |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Simple / Basic | 1D4 | -1 | 2 Hours |
| Advanced / Brew | 2D4 | -1 | 4 Hours |
| Innovated / Tincture | 3D4 | -2 | 8 Hours |
| Ingenious / Suspension | 4D4 | -2 | 12 Hours |
| Cutting Edge / Concoction | 5D4 | -3 | 24 Hours |
| Revolutionary / Solution | 6D4 | -3 | 1 Day |
| Masterwork / Infused | 8D4 | -4 | 2 Days |
| Savant / Elixir | 10D4 | -5 | 2 Days |

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Artificers ever reach true mastery of Reverse Engineering.

These individuals become living archives of craftsmanship, capable of reconstructing forgotten technologies, rediscovering lost formulas, and understanding creations long after their original makers have vanished from history.

Entire guilds have been rebuilt through knowledge recovered by master Reverse Engineers. Ancient designs once thought lost forever have returned to the world because a single Artificer was willing to destroy a masterpiece in order to understand it.

Some call it theft.

Others call it progress.

---

> *"Knowledge belongs to those willing to seek it. Everything else is just ownership."*  
>  **Grand Engineer Tovik Brassbolt**

## Prerequisites
Item Analysis Rank 2

## Scaling
Reverse Engineering rolls and knowledge fragment recovery improve by rank.

## Synergy
Destroys items to learn schematics, formulas, and construction principles.

# Soul Bond Object

## Overview
Soul-bound object stability and capability improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

Through a specialized Soul Engineering ritual, you bind a crafted object to a living soul.

The ritual creates a permanent spiritual connection between the bonded individual and the item, allowing them to sense its condition and whereabouts regardless of distance. While the bond is initially weak, it establishes the foundation for more advanced Soul Engineering techniques.

Most Artificers reserve this process for creations they consider irreplaceable.

A Soul Bond is not ownership.

It is connection.

---

### Effects

- You may create a **Soul Bond** between a willing creature and a crafted item.
- The item must have been personally crafted by you.
- Creating a Soul Bond requires:
  - **25 MP**
  - **1 Measure of Powdered Crystal**
  - **1 Luminous Soul Stone** (Consumed)
- The bonded creature automatically knows:
  - Whether the item exists.
  - Whether the item is damaged or intact.
  - The general direction of the item.
- The bond remains active until:
  - The item is destroyed.
  - The bond is willingly broken.
  - The bonded creature dies.
- Rank 1 Soul Bonds may only be applied to:
  - Mundane Items
  - Non-Enchanted Equipment
  - Non-Enchanted Gadgets
  - Basic Crafted Objects
- Cannot be applied to:
  - Enchanted Items
  - Soul-Bound Items
  - Constructs
  - Relics

---

### Lore

The earliest Soul Engineers believed every crafted object carried a fragment of its creator's essence.

Over time, they discovered methods to strengthen this connection through ritual, Soul Stones, and crystalline catalysts. The result was the first Soul Bonda technique allowing an item and its bearer to remain spiritually connected long after the forge had cooled.

Though simple by modern standards, every advanced Soul Bond begins with this first connection.

---

> *"The strongest creations are not held in the hand. They are carried within the soul."*  
>  **Soulforger Kaelis Voss**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your Soul Bonds grow stronger as your understanding of Soul Engineering deepens.

The connection between bearer and item becomes more precise, allowing the bonded individual to sense not only the direction of the item but also its approximate distance. The bond itself also becomes stable enough to support simple enchanted creations.

What was once a thread becomes a tether.

---

### Effects

- You may create a **Soul Bond** between a willing creature and a crafted item.
- The item must have been personally crafted by you.
- Creating a Soul Bond requires:
  - **35 MP**
  - **1 Measure of Powdered Crystal**
  - **1 Luminous Soul Stone** (Consumed)
- The bonded creature automatically knows:
  - Whether the item exists.
  - Whether the item is damaged or intact.
  - The general direction of the item.
  - The approximate distance to the item.
- The bond remains active until:
  - The item is destroyed.
  - The bond is willingly broken.
  - The bonded creature dies.
- Rank 2 Soul Bonds may be applied to:
  - Mundane Items
  - Non-Enchanted Equipment
  - Non-Enchanted Gadgets
  - Basic Crafted Objects
  - Minor Enchanted Items
  - Charged Items
- Cannot be applied to:
  - Major Enchanted Items
  - Constructs
  - Relics
  - Soul-Bound Items created by another Artificer

---

### Lore

As Soul Engineers refined the art of bonding, they discovered that stronger spiritual links allowed more information to pass between item and bearer.

Direction became distance.

Presence became awareness.

Many merchants, adventurers, and explorers sought out Artificers capable of creating such bonds, as losing a prized possession became far less likely when it could still be sensed across vast distances.

---

> *"A lost item is only lost when the bond can no longer find it."*  
>  **Soulforger Kaelis Voss**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your mastery of Soul Engineering allows the bond between bearer and item to become truly interactive.

The spiritual tether connecting the two has grown strong enough to guide the item back to its bonded owner when called. No longer limited to awareness and tracking, the bond can now exert influence over the item itself, drawing it across the world through the invisible pathways of the soul.

For many Artificers, this is considered the first truly extraordinary application of Soul Bonding.

---

### Effects

- You may create a **Soul Bond** between a willing creature and a crafted item.
- The item must have been personally crafted by you.
- Creating a Soul Bond requires:
  - **50 MP**
  - **1 Measure of Powdered Crystal**
  - **1 Luminous Soul Stone** (Consumed)
- The bonded creature automatically knows:
  - Whether the item exists.
  - Whether the item is damaged or intact.
  - The general direction of the item.
  - The approximate distance to the item.
- Once every **24 Hours**, the bonded creature may attempt to **Recall** the bonded item.
- Recalling a bonded item costs:
  - **25 MP**
  - **5 SP**
- The item instantly returns to the bonded creature if:
  - It is not currently wielded, worn, or held by another creature.
  - It is within the same plane of existence.
  - No magical effect prevents teleportation or summoning.
- Rank 3 Soul Bonds may be applied to:
  - Mundane Items
  - Minor Enchanted Items
  - Moderate Enchanted Items
  - Charged Items
  - Advanced Gadgets
- Cannot be applied to:
  - Major Enchanted Items
  - Constructs
  - Relics
  - Soul-Bound Items created by another Artificer

---

### Lore

The invention of Soul Recall changed Soul Engineering forever.

Before its discovery, Soul Bonds were viewed primarily as tracking tools. Everything changed when an Artificer named Veloran Ashforge accidentally summoned his stolen prototype across an entire kingdom during a moment of desperation.

Since then, countless Artificers have refined the technique, ensuring that their most treasured creations can always find their way home.

Some scholars claim the item travels through space.

Others believe it follows the soul itself.

Regardless of the truth, the result remains the same.

A bonded creation remembers where it belongs.

---

> *"Distance may separate creator and creation, but the soul remembers the path between them."*  
>  **Soulforger Kaelis Voss**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your understanding of Soul Engineering reaches a level where powerful magical creations can safely sustain a Soul Bond.

The connection between bearer and item becomes exceptionally stable, allowing even heavily enchanted objects to maintain a permanent spiritual link without disrupting their magical properties.

At this stage, Soul Bonds are no longer limited to tracking and recall. The bond becomes a conduit through which item and bearer remain constantly connected, regardless of distance.

The item knows its owner.

And its owner knows the item.

---

### Effects

- You may create a **Soul Bond** between a willing creature and a crafted item.
- The item must have been personally crafted by you.
- Creating a Soul Bond requires:
  - **75 MP**
  - **1 Measure of Powdered Crystal**
  - **1 Luminous Soul Stone** (Consumed)
- The bonded creature automatically knows:
  - Whether the item exists.
  - Whether the item is damaged or intact.
  - The general direction of the item.
  - The approximate distance to the item.
- Once every **24 Hours**, the bonded creature may attempt to **Recall** the bonded item.
- Recalling a bonded item costs:
  - **25 MP**
  - **5 SP**
- The item instantly returns to the bonded creature if:
  - It is not currently wielded, worn, or held by another creature.
  - It is within the same plane of existence.
  - No magical effect prevents teleportation or summoning.
- Rank 4 Soul Bonds may be applied to:
  - Mundane Items
  - Minor Enchanted Items
  - Moderate Enchanted Items
  - Major Enchanted Items
  - Charged Items
  - Advanced Gadgets
  - Utility Constructs
  - Combat Constructs
- Cannot be applied to:
  - Mythic Items
  - Legendary Items
  - Relics
  - Soul-Bound Items created by another Artificer

---

### Lore

Many master Artificers consider Rank 4 the true pinnacle of practical Soul Engineering.

The bond is stable enough to survive powerful enchantments, advanced arcane circuitry, and even artificial souls embedded within constructs. Entire guilds have relied upon Soul Bonded equipment to track valuable assets, recover lost inventions, and maintain control over priceless creations.

Few thieves enjoy discovering that the item they stole knows exactly who it belongs to.

---

> *"Ownership is a legal concept. A Soul Bond is a spiritual one."*  
>  **High Soulforger Kaelis Voss**

## Rank 5
### Description

You have mastered the art of Soul Engineering.

The bonds you create transcend ordinary spiritual connections, allowing even the most powerful creations to remain permanently linked to their chosen bearer. Through years of study and experimentation, you have learned how to weave a Soul Bond into legendary works without disrupting their magical or spiritual nature.

The bond becomes more than a tether.

It becomes a living connection between soul and creation.

No matter where the item travels, no matter who possesses it, the bond endures.

---

### Effects

- You may create a **Soul Bond** between a willing creature and a crafted item.
- The item must have been personally crafted by you.
- Creating a Soul Bond requires:
  - **100 MP**
  - **1 Measure of Powdered Crystal**
  - **1 Luminous Soul Stone** (Consumed)
- The bonded creature automatically knows:
  - Whether the item exists.
  - Whether the item is damaged or intact.
  - The general direction of the item.
  - The approximate distance to the item.
- Once every **12 Hours**, the bonded creature may attempt to **Recall** the bonded item.
- Recalling a bonded item costs:
  - **25 MP**
  - **5 SP**
- The item instantly returns to the bonded creature if:
  - It is not currently wielded, worn, or held by another creature.
  - It is within the same plane of existence.
  - No magical effect prevents teleportation or summoning.
- Rank 5 Soul Bonds may be applied to:
  - Mundane Items
  - Minor Enchanted Items
  - Moderate Enchanted Items
  - Major Enchanted Items
  - Mythic Items
  - Legendary Items
  - Charged Items
  - Advanced Gadgets
  - Utility Constructs
  - Combat Constructs
- Cannot be applied to:
  - Relics
  - Soul-Bound Items created by another Artificer

---

### Lore

Only the greatest Soul Engineers ever achieve mastery over Soul Bonding.

Their creations become famous not only for their craftsmanship, but for the enduring connection they share with their owners. Legendary weapons return to their wielders after being lost for decades. Ancient constructs continue serving families generations after their creators have passed.

Many historians believe that some of the world's most famous heirlooms remain intact solely because of the Soul Bonds woven into them.

A masterpiece may outlive its creator.

A Soul Bond ensures it never forgets them.

---

> *"Steel rusts. Enchantments fade. Even legends are forgotten. But a soul remembers."*  
>  **High Soulforger Kaelis Voss**

## Prerequisites
Soul Stone access and Artificer Discipline Rank 3

## Scaling
Soul-bound object stability and capability improve by rank.

## Synergy
Feeds Soul Integration, enchanted item growth, scaling creations, and advanced campaign artifacts.

# Arcane Reactor

## Overview
Reactor capacity, stability, and supported creations improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have learned how to construct and integrate a basic Arcane Reactor.

An Arcane Reactor is a self-contained magical power core designed to generate, store, and regulate arcane energy. Unlike personal mana reserves, reactor energy is dedicated entirely to powering Artificer creations and advanced technologies.

The reactor may be installed within armour, a backpack unit, a construct harness, a prosthetic limb, or another suitable Artificer creation.

Though primitive by later standards, even a Basic Reactor dramatically increases an Artificer's ability to maintain inventions in the field.

---

### Effects

You gain a personal **Arcane Reactor**.

### Reactor Capacity

The reactor can store:

```text
100 Reactor Energy

## Rank 2
### Description

Your Arcane Reactor has undergone significant improvements in both efficiency and storage capacity.

Refined mana channels, improved crystal matrices, and enhanced containment systems allow the reactor to store substantially more energy while maintaining a stable output. Many Artificers begin relying on their reactor as the primary power source for their inventions at this stage.

The reactor no longer feels like an experiment.

It feels like an essential part of your craft.

---

### Effects

You gain an upgraded **Arcane Reactor**.

### Reactor Capacity

The reactor can store:

```text
250 Reactor Energy

## Rank 3
### Description

Your Arcane Reactor has become a highly efficient power core capable of sustaining advanced Artificer technologies for extended periods.

At this level, the reactor is no longer simply a backup energy source. It has become the heart of your inventions, supplying power to constructs, dimensional technologies, soul-forged creations, and advanced magical devices.

Many Artificers view Rank 3 as the point where their reactor becomes a true extension of themselves.

---

### Effects

You gain an upgraded **Arcane Reactor**.

### Reactor Capacity

The reactor can store:

```text
500 Reactor Energy

## Rank 4
### Description

Your Arcane Reactor has evolved into a superior power core capable of sustaining some of the most demanding Artificer technologies.

The reactor now produces enough energy to support multiple active systems simultaneously, allowing advanced constructs, dimensional technologies, soul-forged creations, and experimental devices to operate without constantly draining your personal mana reserves.

Few Artificers possess a reactor of this quality.

Fewer still understand how it truly works.

---

### Effects

You gain an upgraded **Arcane Reactor**.

### Reactor Capacity

The reactor can store:

```text
1,000 Reactor Energy

## Rank 5
### Description

You have perfected the art of Arcane Reactor design.

Your reactor is no longer merely a power source. It is a self-sustaining arcane engine capable of generating immense quantities of energy for your inventions, constructs, dimensional technologies, and soul-forged creations.

Many master Artificers spend decades attempting to create a reactor of this quality. Those who succeed often become capable of sustaining technologies that rival the magical infrastructure of entire kingdoms.

The reactor has become the heart of your craft.

You gain a **Grand Arcane Reactor**.

### Reactor Capacity

The reactor can store:

2,000 Reactor Energy

# Dimensional Warehouse

## Overview
Dimensional storage capacity and safety improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have learned how to anchor a small extradimensional space to reality.

By creating a temporary dimensional gateway, you may access a private storage chamber existing outside the normal world. This chamber serves as a secure repository for valuable materials, equipment, resources, and treasures.

At Rank 1, the warehouse is little more than a dimensional shack, but it represents the foundation of a far greater storage network.

Only the creator may access the warehouse.

The door appears where you choose, taking a form influenced by your personality, magical style, and crafting methods.

---

### Effects

You gain access to a personal extradimensional storage space known as a **Dimensional Warehouse**.

### Activation

- Spend **100 MP**.
- Create a dimensional doorway within **3m**.
- The doorway remains open for **10 Minutes**.
- The doorway may be dismissed early at any time.
- The warehouse persists permanently between uses.

6m  6m  3m

The small storage shack you once maintained has expanded into a dedicated dimensional storage facility, allowing you to safely store larger quantities of equipment, materials, and resources. While still inaccessible to others, the warehouse has become far more practical for an active Artificer.

# Scaling Creation

## Overview
Allows creations to improve through investment, soul energy, or campaign progression.

## Rank 1
### Description

Most crafted items reach their peak the moment they are completed.

You have discovered a method to create items capable of growth.

By binding a soul into a carefully prepared vessel, you may create a **Scalable Item**, a creation capable of evolving over time as its power develops. The soul acts as an Evolution Core, providing the item with the ability to adapt and unlock new potential.

This process is dangerous.

Not every soul willingly accepts imprisonment.

A failed binding can awaken the soul within the item, creating an unpredictable relationship between creator, wielder, and creation.

---

### Effects

You may create **Scalable Items**.

A Scalable Item is a crafted item capable of gaining additional ranks after creation.

### Requirements

To create a Scalable Item, all of the following are required:

- Item must be **Unusual Item Class or higher**
- One **Luminous Soul Stone** (minimum)
- Appropriate crafting materials
- Relevant schematic
- Access to the required crafting profession
- Completion of a Soul Binding Ritual

### Creation Costs

During creation consume:

- 100 MP
- 1 Luminous Soul Stone
- Normal crafting materials

### Scaling Capacity

Rank 1 Scalable Items may possess:

- **2 Evolution Ranks**
- Base Item Rank + 1 additional Evolution Rank

Example:

```text
Evolution Rank I
Evolution Rank II

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of soul-forging has improved considerably.

You can now create more stable Evolution Cores, allowing scalable items to progress further along their evolutionary path. Stronger souls may be bound into suitable vessels, granting access to greater potential and more complex growth patterns.

Despite your growing mastery, the soul remains an independent existence. Every binding still carries the risk of awakening something that was never meant to remain trapped.

---

### Effects

You may create **Scalable Items**.

A Scalable Item is a crafted item capable of gaining additional ranks after creation.

### Requirements

To create a Scalable Item, all of the following are required:

At this stage, every scalable item becomes unique.

No two souls evolve in exactly the same way.

At this level, the soul bound within a scalable item begins to exert a far greater influence over its growth and development. Powerful souls may unlock unique evolution branches unavailable to ordinary creations, causing no two scalable items to develop in exactly the same way.

Many master Artificers consider Rank 4 the point where a scalable item becomes a true companion rather than a tool.

The soul no longer merely fuels growth.

It helps shape it.

# Arcane Exchange

## Overview
Transmutation scope, safety, and value ceiling improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have learned the first principles of Arcane Exchange, an ancient Artificer discipline based upon the law of equivalent exchange.

Through the use of mana, physical exertion, and soul catalysts, you may alter the structure of materials and convert them into related substances. While powerful, Arcane Exchange cannot create matter from nothing. Every exchange requires sacrifice, and the value of the resulting material can never exceed the value of the materials consumed.

At Rank 1, you can only safely transmute simple and common materials.

---

### Effects

You may perform a material transmutation through Arcane Exchange.

### Exchange Cost

Each exchange requires:

- 100 MP
- 25 SP
- Soul Stone 
- Target Materials

### Exchange Check

Make an **Wisdom Check**.

Gain:
+2 Arcane Exchange Bonus

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of Arcane Exchange has expanded beyond simple material conversion.

You can now manipulate more advanced material structures, allowing the transmutation of uncommon substances and refined crafting resources. Through greater control of mana flow and soul catalysts, you can maintain the integrity of more complex materials during the exchange process.

While still bound by the laws of equivalent exchange, your ability to reshape matter has become significantly more versatile.

---

### Effects

You may perform a material transmutation through Arcane Exchange.

### Exchange Cost

Each exchange requires:

- 150 MP
- 40 SP
- Brilliant Soul Stone 
- Target Materials

### Exchange Check

Make an **Intelligence Check**.

Gain: +4 Arcane Exchange Bonus

## Rank 3
### Description

Your mastery of Arcane Exchange now extends into the realm of rare materials.

You can manipulate complex material structures, refine exotic resources, and perform transmutations that many craftsmen consider impossible. At this level, the Artificer begins to understand that materials are merely different arrangements of the same fundamental building blocks.

Rare materials remain difficult to control, however, and even minor mistakes can trigger catastrophic transmutation failures.

The greater the value of the material, the greater the price demanded by the universe.

---

### Effects

You may perform a material transmutation through Arcane Exchange.

### Exchange Cost

Each exchange requires:

- 250 MP
- 60 SP
- 1 Measure of Special Soul Stone Dust
- Target Materials

### Exchange Check

Make an **Intelligence Check**.

Gain:

```text
+6 Arcane Exchange Bonus

## Rank 4
### Description

You have achieved mastery over advanced transmutation principles.

Epic and Mythic materials now fall within your understanding, allowing you to reshape substances that many believe immutable. Your Arcane Exchange calculations have become increasingly refined, enabling large-scale conversions while maintaining material integrity.

The universe still demands equivalent value.

You have simply become better at understanding the exchange.

---

### Effects

You may perform a material transmutation through Arcane Exchange.

### Exchange Cost

Each exchange requires:

- 400 MP
- 100 SP
- 1 Measure of Resplendent Soul Stone Dust
- Target Materials

### Exchange Check

Make an **Intelligence Check**.

Gain:

```text
+8 Arcane Exchange Bonusv

## Rank 5
### Description

You have mastered the ultimate principles of Arcane Exchange.

Legendary and Relic materials now fall within the limits of your understanding. Through overwhelming mana output, immense physical effort, and powerful soul catalysts, you can alter materials once believed impossible to transmute.

Few Artificers in history have reached this level.

Those who do become known as Grand Transmuters, individuals capable of reshaping entire industries through mastery of matter itself.

Yet even now, one law remains absolute.

Nothing is free.

Everything has a cost.

---

### Effects

You may perform a material transmutation through Arcane Exchange.

### Exchange Cost

Each exchange requires:

- 750 MP
- 150 SP
- 1 Measure of Resplendent Soul Stone Dust
- Target Materials

### Exchange Check

Make an **Intelligence Check**.

Gain:

```text
+10 Arcane Exchange Bonus

## Prerequisites
Arcane Reactor Rank 4 or Scaling Creation Rank 4

## Scaling
Transmutation scope, safety, and value ceiling improve by rank.

## Synergy
Material transmutation based on equivalent exchange; connects to crafting, soul catalysts, and rare materials.

# Portable Structure

## Overview
Portable structure size, deployment stability, and complexity improve by rank.

## Rank 1
### Description

You have mastered the first principles of Structural Compression.

By combining dimensional engineering, arcane transmutation, and spatial stabilization, you can compress an entire building into a compact portable form without damaging the structure itself.

Once compressed, the structure becomes a small object approximately 10cm  10cm in size, allowing it to be carried, transported, stored, or secured until needed.

The building remains fully intact while compressed and may be redeployed at any time provided sufficient space exists.

---

### Effects

You may convert a completed building into a **Portable Structure**.

### Compression Cost

Compressing a structure requires:

- 500 MP
- 100 SP
- 1 Measure of Resplendent Soul Stone Dust
- Physical contact with the structure

---

### Portable Form

Upon successful compression:

The building transforms into a portable object approximately:

```text
10cm  10cm  10cm

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of Structural Compression has advanced considerably.

You can now compress and transport entire large buildings while preserving their internal contents, furnishings, and layout. The compression matrix has become significantly more stable, allowing larger structures to survive repeated deployments without suffering dimensional stress.

Many Artificers begin using Portable Structures as mobile headquarters, allowing them to relocate their operations whenever necessary.

---

### Effects

You may convert a completed building into a **Portable Structure**.

### Compression Cost

Compressing a structure requires:

- 750 MP
- 150 SP
- 1 Measure of Resplendent Soul Stone Dust
- Physical contact with the structure

---

### Portable Form

Upon successful compression:

The building transforms into a portable object approximately:

```text
10cm  10cm  10cm

## Rank 3
### Description

Your mastery of Structural Compression now extends beyond individual buildings.

You can compress entire compounds into a portable form while preserving every structure, pathway, wall, furnishing, and stored item within the property. The dimensional matrix becomes powerful enough to maintain multiple buildings as a single compressed entity.

Many master merchants, military engineers, and adventuring organizations would consider such technology priceless.

A settlement that can travel is no longer bound by geography.

---

### Effects

You may convert a completed compound into a **Portable Structure**.

### Compression Cost

Compressing a structure requires:

- 1,000 MP
- 250 SP
- 1 Resplendent Soul Stone
- Physical contact with the compound's central structure

---

### Portable Form

Upon successful compression:

The compound transforms into a portable object approximately:

```text
10cm  10cm  10cm

## Rank 4
### Description

Your mastery of Structural Compression has reached extraordinary heights.

You can now compress entire manors and estates into a portable form while preserving every room, furnishing, security system, vault, garden, and structure contained within the property.

At this level, Portable Structure ceases to be a transportation tool and becomes a method of relocating entire lifestyles.

Many nobles, guild masters, and wealthy merchants would pay fortunes for such a capability.

Most Artificers capable of this simply build their own estates instead.

---

### Effects

You may convert a completed manor into a **Portable Structure**.

### Compression Cost

Compressing a structure requires:

- 1,500 MP
- 400 SP
- 1 Resplendent Soul Stone
- Physical contact with the manor's central structure

---

### Portable Form

Upon successful compression:

The manor transforms into a portable object approximately:

```text
10cm  10cm  10cm

## Rank 5
### Description

You have achieved the pinnacle of Structural Compression.

The limitations of conventional architecture no longer apply to your understanding. Through advanced dimensional engineering, arcane stabilization, and reality-binding techniques, you can compress structures infused with powerful magical energies.

Mage towers, enchanted fortresses, floating structures, dimensional facilities, and other magical constructions may now be transformed into portable forms and transported across the world.

Among Artificers, this achievement is considered one of the greatest feats of engineering ever conceived.

Entire magical civilizations have been preserved through Portable Structures of this caliber.

---

### Effects

You may convert a completed magical structure into a **Portable Structure**.

### Compression Cost

Compressing a structure requires:

- 2,500 MP
- 750 SP
- 1 Resplendent Soul Stone
- 1 Measure of Resplendent Soul Stone Dust
- Physical contact with the structure's core or anchor point

---

### Portable Form

Upon successful compression:

The structure transforms into a portable object approximately:

```text
10cm  10cm  10cm

## Prerequisites
Dimensional Warehouse Rank 4

## Synergy
Turns Artificer logistics into shelters, mobile workshops, field bases, and campaign infrastructure.

entries.body:
# Blood Rite

## Overview
Blood Rite is the first Sangramancy technique taught to every Bloodhunter. By willingly shedding their own blood, a Bloodhunter awakens the latent magical energy carried within it, binding their life force directly to a chosen weapon. This ritual transforms an ordinary weapon into a conduit of blood magic, allowing every strike to carry supernatural power.

Unlike traditional enchantments fuelled by mana, Blood Rite demands sacrifice. The Bloodhunter must willingly wound themselves, offering part of their own vitality to awaken the rite. This sacrifice is never symbolic—the pain is real, and every activation reminds the Bloodhunter that true power always demands a price.

As the ritual takes hold, crimson runes spread across the weapon before sinking beneath its surface. To outsiders the weapon appears stained with fresh blood, while those capable of sensing magic witness violent currents of crimson energy flowing through the steel. Each strike tears not only flesh but also the life essence of the target, leaving wounds that continue to bleed long after the blow has landed.

Although Blood Rite is considered the most fundamental Sangramancy technique, mastering it is a lifelong pursuit. Every future Bloodhunter ability builds upon the discipline, sacrifice, and control first learned through this ritual.

## Rank 1
### Description

Blood Rite is the first Sangramancy technique taught to every Bloodhunter. By willingly shedding their own blood, a Bloodhunter awakens the latent magical energy carried within it, binding their life force directly to a chosen weapon. This ritual transforms an ordinary weapon into a conduit of blood magic, allowing every strike to carry supernatural power.

Unlike traditional enchantments fuelled by mana, Blood Rite demands sacrifice. The Bloodhunter must willingly wound themselves, offering part of their own vitality to awaken the rite. This sacrifice is never symbolic—the pain is real, and every activation reminds the Bloodhunter that true power always demands a price.

As the ritual takes hold, crimson runes spread across the weapon before sinking beneath its surface. To outsiders the weapon appears stained with fresh blood, while those capable of sensing magic witness violent currents of crimson energy flowing through the steel. Each strike tears not only flesh but also the life essence of the target, leaving wounds that continue to bleed long after the blow has landed.

Although Blood Rite is considered the most fundamental Sangramancy technique, mastering it is a lifelong pursuit. Every future Bloodhunter ability builds upon the discipline, sacrifice, and control first learned through this ritual.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, you may activate Blood Rite by sacrificing **5 HP**.
- Activating Blood Rite generates **5 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Blood Rite may be activated **twice per Long Rest**.
- Choose one weapon you are currently wielding.
- The chosen weapon becomes empowered with Sangramancy for **3 Combat Rounds**.
- While Blood Rite is active, the weapon deals an additional **1d6 Blood Damage** on each successful hit.
- The first successful attack against a creature each turn inflicts **Minor Bleeding**.
- Minor Bleeding deals **1d4 Blood Damage** at the start of the target's next **2 turns**.
- Reapplying Minor Bleeding refreshes its duration but does not increase its damage.
- Blood Damage dealt by Blood Rite is considered **Magical Damage**.
- Only one Blood Rite may be active at a time.
- Blood Rite immediately ends if the empowered weapon leaves your possession for more than one round.
- Blood Rite may be dismissed at any time without requiring an action.

### Lore

The first Blood Rite is remembered by every Bloodhunter. It is the moment they cease relying solely upon steel and instead place their trust in their own life force. The scar left by the ritual is traditionally never healed through magic, serving as a permanent reminder that Sangramancy is founded upon sacrifice.

Among veteran Bloodhunters, Blood Rite is often described as a conversation between the hunter and the blood itself. Every activation stirs the countless emotions carried within their lifeblood—anger, grief, determination, fear, and vengeance. With each use, these emotions linger as Blood Points, slowly testing the hunter's resolve.

Those who fail to respect the burden of Sangramancy eventually lose themselves to Bloodlust. Those who endure learn that the true enemy is not the monster before them, but the darkness growing within.

> *"The first lesson of Sangramancy is not how to bleed. It is how to stop the blood from commanding you."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 2
### Description

Having survived the first teachings of Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter learns to deepen their Blood Rite by sacrificing more of their own vitality. The additional blood offered strengthens the bond between hunter and weapon, allowing the crimson energy to remain stable for longer while striking with greater consistency.

At this stage, the Bloodhunter begins to understand that Blood Rite is not merely an enchantment but a living extension of their own emotions. Every heartbeat fuels the rite, every wound strengthens it, and every enemy struck feeds the growing resonance within their soul. What once felt like an act of desperation slowly becomes a deliberate act of discipline.

Veteran Bloodhunters teach that Rank II is where complacency becomes the greatest danger. The rite feels more natural to invoke, tempting hunters to rely upon its power in every battle. Those who forget that every activation feeds the growing burden of Blood Points often discover too late that Sangramancy demands payment long after the battle has ended.

Although the increased sacrifice grants greater control over the rite, it also draws stronger emotional echoes from the Bloodhunter's blood. Mastery lies not in resisting these emotions, but in acknowledging them without allowing them to take control.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, you may activate Blood Rite by sacrificing **8 HP**.
- Activating Blood Rite generates **6 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Blood Rite may be activated **twice per Long Rest**.
- Choose one weapon you are currently wielding.
- The chosen weapon becomes empowered with Sangramancy for **4 Combat Rounds**.
- While Blood Rite is active, the weapon deals an additional **1d6 Blood Damage** on each successful hit.
- The first successful attack against a creature each turn inflicts **Minor Bleeding**.
- Minor Bleeding deals **1d4 Blood Damage** at the start of the target's next **3 turns**.
- Reapplying Minor Bleeding refreshes its duration but does not increase its damage.
- Blood Damage dealt by Blood Rite is considered **Magical Damage**.
- Only one Blood Rite may be active at a time.
- Blood Rite immediately ends if the empowered weapon leaves your possession for more than one round.
- Blood Rite may be dismissed at any time without requiring an action.

### Lore

Every Bloodhunter remembers the first time they willingly shed more blood than was necessary. It is a difficult lesson to accept that greater strength can only be achieved through greater sacrifice. Many abandon their training at this stage, believing the cost too high to justify the power gained.

Those who continue soon realise that Sangramancy is not testing their endurance—it is testing their resolve. Every wound inflicted upon themselves becomes another promise that innocent lives will not bear the burden instead.

Within the Bloodhunter Orders, the scars earned through repeated Blood Rites are known as the Crimson Oath. They are proof that the hunter has chosen duty over comfort and sacrifice over fear, even while the growing weight of Blood Points whispers constantly from within.

> *"Power offered freely is rarely understood. Power bought with your own blood is never forgotten."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 3
### Description

Blood Rite reaches a turning point at Rank III. No longer simply a ritual of sacrifice, it becomes a true extension of the Bloodhunter's will. The blood willingly spilled no longer merely empowers a weapon—it answers the call of its master, surging through the blade with controlled ferocity. The hunter has begun to understand that Sangramancy is not about commanding blood, but existing in harmony with the emotions carried within it.

As mastery grows, so too does the burden placed upon both body and mind. The Bloodhunter can invoke Blood Rite more frequently than before, yet every activation draws increasingly powerful emotional echoes into their soul. Hatred, grief, vengeance, and fear all linger within the growing pool of Blood Points, testing the hunter's discipline with every battle.

Veterans warn that Rank III is where many Bloodhunters fall. The rite becomes dependable enough to use in nearly every encounter, creating the dangerous illusion that Sangramancy has finally been mastered. Those who grow overconfident often discover that the blood remembers every sacrifice ever made, and eventually demands to be heard.

Only those who remain disciplined can continue walking the path without surrendering themselves to Bloodlust.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, you may activate Blood Rite by sacrificing **12 HP**.
- Activating Blood Rite generates **8 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Blood Rite may be activated **3 times per Short Rest**.
- Choose one weapon you are currently wielding.
- The chosen weapon becomes empowered with Sangramancy for **5 Combat Rounds**.
- While Blood Rite is active, the weapon deals an additional **1d8 Blood Damage** on each successful hit.
- The first successful attack against a creature each turn inflicts **Moderate Bleeding**.
- Moderate Bleeding deals **1d6 Blood Damage** at the start of the target's next **3 turns**.
- Reapplying Moderate Bleeding refreshes its duration but does not stack its damage.
- Blood Damage dealt by Blood Rite is considered **Magical Damage**.
- Only one Blood Rite may be active at a time.
- Blood Rite immediately ends if the empowered weapon leaves your possession for more than one round.
- Blood Rite may be dismissed at any time without requiring an action.

### Lore

Within every Bloodhunter Order, Rank III is known as the Threshold. It marks the point where apprentices become true hunters, trusted to undertake contracts without constant supervision. The ability to invoke Blood Rite repeatedly is seen as a privilege earned through discipline rather than a reward for strength alone.

Senior Bloodhunters teach that every drop of blood used in Sangramancy leaves behind an emotional imprint. Over time these echoes begin to accumulate, speaking louder with every battle. Some hunters describe hearing whispers at the edge of their thoughts, while others experience an unsettling calm that precedes Bloodlust.

Those who survive this stage emerge with a newfound respect for Sangramancy. They realise that true mastery will never come from greater power alone, but from maintaining control when every instinct urges them to surrender to the blood.

> *"The blood grows louder with every battle. Mastery is not silencing it—it is refusing to answer its call."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 4
### Description

By the time a Bloodhunter attains the Fourth Rank of Blood Rite, Sangramancy has become second nature. The ritual no longer requires hesitation or careful preparation. The Bloodhunter instinctively understands how much blood must be sacrificed, allowing them to awaken the rite with frightening speed and unwavering precision.

The blood flowing through their veins has become increasingly responsive to their will. Crimson energy surges across their weapon with greater intensity than ever before, carving glowing runes into the air as each strike lands. Wounds inflicted by the empowered weapon refuse to close naturally, leaving enemies weakened by relentless blood loss while the Bloodhunter presses their advantage.

Yet this level of mastery comes with an equally dangerous burden. The greater sacrifice required to sustain such power causes Blood Points to accumulate at an alarming rate. Veteran Bloodhunters often describe this stage as walking beside a predator that is forever watching, waiting patiently for a single lapse in discipline before seizing control.

Only the most disciplined hunters can maintain such power repeatedly without surrendering to Bloodlust. Every battle becomes a contest between the Bloodhunter's will and the countless emotions awakened through Sangramancy.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, you may activate Blood Rite by sacrificing **16 HP**.
- Activating Blood Rite generates **10 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Blood Rite may be activated **3 times per Short Rest**.
- Choose one weapon you are currently wielding.
- The chosen weapon becomes empowered with Sangramancy for **6 Combat Rounds**.
- While Blood Rite is active, the weapon deals an additional **1d8 Blood Damage** on each successful hit.
- The first successful attack against a creature each turn inflicts **Major Bleeding**.
- Major Bleeding deals **1d8 Blood Damage** at the start of the target's next **3 turns**.
- Reapplying Major Bleeding refreshes its duration but does not stack its damage.
- Blood Damage dealt by Blood Rite is considered **Magical Damage**.
- Only one Blood Rite may be active at a time.
- Blood Rite immediately ends if the empowered weapon leaves your possession for more than one round.
- Blood Rite may be dismissed at any time without requiring an action.

### Lore

Among Bloodhunter Orders, reaching the Fourth Rank is a moment of both celebration and concern. It is proof that the hunter has survived countless battles and mastered techniques that would have claimed the lives of lesser practitioners. Yet it is also the stage where the greatest number of Bloodhunters are lost—not to monsters, but to themselves.

Masters teach that Sangramancy is never truly controlled. Instead, it is respected. Every ritual strengthens the bond between hunter and blood, but every ritual also strengthens the emotions dwelling within that blood. Those who mistake confidence for mastery often discover too late that Bloodlust has been quietly growing beneath the surface all along.

The wisest Bloodhunters learn that restraint is every bit as important as power. A hunter who knows when **not** to invoke Blood Rite is often far more dangerous than one who wields it without hesitation.

> *"The strongest Bloodhunter is not the one who bleeds the most... but the one who knows exactly when another drop is too much."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 5
### Description

Blood Rite has reached its ultimate form. The Bloodhunter has become one of the few living masters capable of wielding Sangramancy without hesitation, instinctively weaving blood magic into every movement of battle. The ritual that once demanded complete concentration has become as natural as drawing breath, allowing the Bloodhunter to invoke it repeatedly throughout even the longest encounters.

The sacrifice demanded is immense. A master Bloodhunter willingly opens a grievous wound to unleash overwhelming power, allowing the blood itself to flood their weapon with ancient crimson energy. Every heartbeat fuels the rite, every strike carries devastating force, and every wound inflicted leaves behind echoes of suffering that refuse to fade.

Yet no Bloodhunter ever escapes the price of Sangramancy. While others see only unmatched skill, the master knows that each activation pushes them closer to Bloodlust. Their greater understanding has not silenced the emotions carried within the blood—it has merely allowed them to shoulder a far heavier burden before those emotions threaten to consume them.

Only the greatest Bloodhunters in history have achieved this level of mastery. Their names are remembered not because they wielded Blood Rite more powerfully than anyone else, but because they stood upon the edge of Bloodlust countless times and never surrendered their humanity.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, you may activate Blood Rite by sacrificing **20 HP**.
- Activating Blood Rite generates **15 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Blood Rite may be activated **4 times per Combat**.
- Choose one weapon you are currently wielding.
- The chosen weapon becomes empowered with Sangramancy for **8 Combat Rounds**.
- While Blood Rite is active, the weapon deals an additional **1d10 Blood Damage** on each successful hit.
- The first successful attack against a creature each turn inflicts **Severe Bleeding**.
- Severe Bleeding deals **1d10 Blood Damage** at the start of the target's next **4 turns**.
- Reapplying Severe Bleeding refreshes its duration but does not stack its damage.
- Blood Damage dealt by Blood Rite is considered **Magical Damage**.
- While Blood Rite is active, your weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistances and immunities.
- Only one Blood Rite may be active at a time.
- Blood Rite immediately ends if the empowered weapon leaves your possession for more than one round.
- Blood Rite may be dismissed at any time without requiring an action.

### Lore

Among Bloodhunters, Rank V Blood Rite is regarded as the pinnacle of Sangramancy. Very few survive long enough to achieve it, and fewer still possess the discipline required to wield such immense power responsibly. Those who do are often feared as much as the monsters they hunt, for the line separating hunter and horror has become dangerously thin.

The greatest masters teach that Sangramancy is not a battle against Bloodlust, but a lifelong negotiation with it. Every ritual, every sacrifice, and every drop of blood strengthens both the hunter and the darkness waiting within. Those who believe they have conquered Bloodlust have already begun to lose themselves.

Legends tell of Bloodhunters who stood alone against dragons, demon lords, and ancient horrors, their weapons burning crimson until the battlefield itself became stained with blood. Survivors rarely remembered what those hunters said during the battle. They remembered only the terrifying silence, the precise movements, and the overwhelming certainty that death had come—not as a raging beast, but as a calm and methodical executioner.

> *"Mastery is not reaching the edge of Bloodlust. Mastery is standing upon its edge, hearing it whisper your name... and choosing to take one more step forward without falling."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor
